issues.issue: Securities count as 'Foreign Securities' if 'principally cleared and settled outside the United States', and 'principally' is given no measure although the label switches the default interest rate under Sections 13.1 and 13.2.
The definition breaks off mid-sentence at 'if at least two such rates appear, the arithmetic mean of', so the fallback rate-setting mechanic is incomplete as written.
The definition omits the section number entirely ('shall have the meaning assigned in Section'), leaving the cross-reference blank.

Absent agreement the Margin Notice Deadline is 'the deadline for such purposes established in accordance with market practice', an unfixed external standard that determines whether margin must be met the same day or the next.

The floor is 100% 'unless (a) Borrower and Lender agree otherwise ... and (b) Lender is not a Customer', so it is unclear whether both conditions must be satisfied to displace the floor and what percentage applies if only one is.
Schedule B section 6 purports to restate 'Margin Percentage' with different figures, so the operative percentage depends on reconciling this definition with that Schedule provision.

Where Annex II or another writing does not apply, Market Value is set 'in accordance with market practice' from 'a generally recognized source agreed to by the parties', leaving the valuation of collateral and loaned securities to an unfixed standard.

The definition says its determinations apply 'for all purposes under this Agreement, except for purposes of Section 13', yet Section 13 itself measures damages by Market Value concepts and prices from 'a generally recognized source', so the carve-out leaves the default valuation rule unstated.
'Retransfer' is defined by a list of specific dealings closing with the general 'or otherwise transfer such Collateral', leaving the catch-all's reach against the enumerated acts open.

'Securities' is defined circularly as 'securities or, if agreed by the parties in writing, other assets', which supplies no boundary and lets the central subject matter of the Agreement be anything the parties write down.

The characterisation is qualified by 'except insofar as the type of assets subject to the Loan would render such definition inapplicable', a self-cancelling proviso that leaves the status of any given Loan to be decided later.

The disclosure tells Lender that the Collateral delivered may be its only source of satisfaction if Borrower fails to return the Loaned Securities, which pulls against Section 13.1, under which Borrower remains personally liable for any excess and grants Lender a security interest in its other property.

Agent must supply 'such information in its possession necessary to complete all required fields in the format generally used in the industry' and use 'best efforts' as to optional information, warranting accuracy only 'to the best of its knowledge' and excepting 'pseudo tax identification numbers' — a cluster of unfixed standards.

The provision limits Agent's liability and provides that Agent is not to be treated or liable as principal, but its wording is so degraded that the scope of the limitation — which representations it covers and which obligations survive — cannot be fixed from the text.

The limitation of Agent's liability pulls against Section 11.1(a), under which each party agrees either to be liable as principal or to comply with the agency Annex, and against Agent's own continuing representations in Annex I-A section 1.

Treating each Principal's allocable portion as a separate Loan, with obligations determined Principal by Principal, is hard to reconcile with Section 18, which makes all Loans a single relationship with cross-default and cross-Loan set-off.

The clause substitutes 'Principal' for 'Lender' and 'other party' throughout the Agreement, but the text is so degraded that which references are converted, and which rights remain with Agent, cannot be determined from the words.

The listed-securities valuation rule (last sale price, consolidated tape, preceding Close of Trading) is rendered in text so garbled that the operative pricing sequence cannot be read off the provision.

The rule for securities not listed on an exchange rests on 'market practice' and a 'generally recognized source' agreed by the parties, and as written the text is too corrupted to identify the applicable quotation.

Annex II states that its Market Value determinations apply for all purposes of the Agreement 'except for purposes of Section 13', which leaves the valuation standard for the very remedies in Section 13 to be supplied from elsewhere.

The Annex applies to Equity Securities only if a Loan is designated a Term Loan, but makes 'All Loans of Securities other than Equity Securities' Term Loans by default 'unless otherwise agreed', an asymmetric default whose reach over ordinary open loans is not obvious.

The parties must 'use their best efforts to negotiate in good faith' a Replacement Loan of 'comparable or other Securities' 'mutually agreed upon' — an agreement to agree whose breach cannot be measured against any stated criterion.

Imposing a Breakage Fee on 'the party requesting termination' sits against Section 6.1, which lets either party terminate a Loan on notice without charge, and against Annex III section 2, which preserves the Agreement's termination rights for Term Loans.

The Breakage Fee formula — the components of the 'sum of' and how loss on the replacement transaction is measured — is unreadable as written, so the amount payable cannot be computed from the provision.
The list of incorporated annexes names 'Annex I-A (Agency Annex)', whereas Section 11.1(b) and Section 10.3 condition agency status on executing and complying with 'Annex I'.

Schedule B gives itself priority over the Agreement, while Section 2.1 gives the Agreement priority over an unexecuted Confirmation, so the relative rank of Schedule, Agreement and Confirmation is never completely ordered.

The clause binds the parties to 'any uniform practices applicable to securities loans' among members of two named associations, 'as currently in effect, or successor provisions thereto', and only 'to the extent that such market practice ... does not conflict with the terms of the Agreement' — an open-ended incorporation with an undefined conflict test.

The no-reliance representation is preserved only in fragments ('not relying on any communication ... as investment advice or ... except as expressly set forth in the Agreement'), so the scope of what each party disclaims reliance on cannot be fixed from the text.

The independent-judgment representation survives only as a fragment referring to 'its own decisions regarding' the transactions 'based upon its own judgment and upon advice from such advisers as it deemed necessary', leaving what was represented indeterminate.
The representation that each party 'understands the terms, conditions and risks of each Loan' and is 'willing and able to assume' them is both a vague standard and, as reproduced, incomplete.

Schedule B section 6 rewrites 'Margin Percentage' (with different percentages for different securities) in terms that cannot be squared with the not-less-than-100% definition in Section 25.37, leaving the collateral level to depend on which text governs.
